card.name: Skolt Sami quadrille
card.era: Adopted from Russia/Karelia in the later 19th c.; very popular until WWII; danced to ~1950s; revitalized from the 1970s
card.tagline: The Skolt Sami's emblematic set dance of Russian-Karelian origin.
card.profile: The Skolt Sami quadrille (kolttakatrilli) is a square/set dance of the Skolt Sami, an Orthodox Christian Sami group originally from the Petsamo region (Suonikyla) and resettled after WWII around Sevettijarvi in Inari, NE Finland (Hoppu; kolttasaamelaiset.fi). Sharing much with Karelian and Northern Russian dance culture, it reached the Skolts in the latter 19th century and was historically danced at weddings and festivities to the accordion, harmonica or singing (Hoppu; Yle). Its figures resemble the Karelian katrilli - circles, vis-a-vis, place-changes - and may include a male improvisation showing skill (ripaska). After the evacuation, the community scattered along the Sevettijarvi road, the accordions were left behind in Petsamo, and the dance nearly fell into oblivion before its revival.
card.insight: Petri Hoppu writes that the quadrille is the best known of the Skolts' dances and, perhaps more than any other, has become emblematic of their ethnic identity; from the 1970s the Skolts began to actively revitalize their dances, establishing a quadrille performing group in Sevettijarvi as part of a Sami cultural renaissance (Hoppu, 'Rewriting Skolt Sami Dance History').
